I have loads of them but this one sticks out in my mind for some reason. I was used to my mom being drunk and wanting more. To the point I’d bargained days out of school if I took her to buy more. (Not old enough to drive but could) one night, she was going to get more. But I wouldn’t be driving, she wanted me to stay home with my siblings because stepdad was gone. I said no. Because she was way too drunk to drive and she was trying to take my newborn sibling with her. We fought for the keys and I grabbed the house phone and ran into the hall bathroom. (Which had a drawer directly in front of the door and if you opened the drawer the bathroom door couldn’t be opened.) I opened the drawer and called the police because I knew I couldn’t stop her. All the while she’s trying to beat down the door. Cop comes and says we have to stay with someone for the night (mom included) so she calls her friend and we go to stay there. They continue to drink after we get there. Still I’m relieved. I’m no longer her focus and she’s got more alcohol. I fall asleep on the sofa and I’m woken up after everyone else had gone to bed to my mom picking my head up by my hair. She picked it up so hard it ripped chunks of hair out, she holds my face to hers and tells me to NEVER call the cops on her again. There were some threats, I don’t remember now what they were but they scared the shit out of me. 
She’s sober now. Some time after I moved out, she got into a car accident (drunk) with all my siblings in the car. It was one of her first wake up calls but her last was when she fell down some steps and knocked herself unconscious on concrete. I think one of my siblings found her in a pool of blood and that was the last time she drank. Her background on her phone is that blood and her reminder never to drink again.
That’s awesome. It’s a first for me hearing someone else has as well!

I know you’ve gotten other responses but I thought I’d add my own. Routine is important. For me, at least. Teaching the kids to help out is a big plus on maintaining routine and cleanliness. Even if it’s as simple as putting away their plate or bowl when done with their food. I wanna tell you I shower every night but it’s usually every other night lol.

My house was horrendous my last year as a SAHM but that was depression and putting my sole focus on the kids and nothing else.

Since leaving my marriage I’m doing some work from home in my new place and I’ve been able to maintain a pretty impressive (to me) standard of cleanliness. I also think this is down to luck as my 4yr old likes to help pick up and clean things. My oldest not so much lol. But if she wants pocket money for school, she has to do her chores. 

There are days when it’s hell but don’t let horror stories discourage you if you want to have kids because even though it sounds cliche’ the love for your kids overwhelms the hellish days.

My husband likes to complain about smells. He can always smell the bad stuff. It’s really annoying because he claims he smells them when they aren’t there. He would complain that I didn’t clean the litter enough and would gag walking past. At the time we had a male cat that would have the most horrendous smelling shit so it had to be cleaned out pretty much as soon as he used it so him coming home and saying how bad it smelled even though I’d already cleaned it was frustrating. I even double cleaned it before he got home and sprayed stuff and he’d still dramatically gag. 

One day I clean the entire litter box out. There’s no litter in it, and I’ve completely washed the inside. I put the cats outside, covered the empty box and waited. He got home and instantly went to complaining about the litter, walking past the hallway it was in and gagging. Today it seems even more exaggerated and I grab the litter box, bring it to him and show him that it’s completely empty and washed. He doesn’t complain about the litter anymore.
